item.title: Vodafone Super Deans Eliminations: Nasinu stuns Holy Cross with second-half comeback
item.description: Nasinu Secondary School's Under-18 team produced a remarkable comeback, overturning a 17-0 half-time deficit to defeat Holy Cross College 21-20 in the Vodafone Super Deans Eliminations Competition in Suva today. Holy Cross College dominated the opening half, putting pressure on the Southern Zone finalists from the first whistle and taking a commanding 17-0 lead into the break.
item.content:encoded:
Nasinu Secondary School's Under-18 team produced a remarkable comeback, overturning a 17-0 half-time deficit to defeat Holy Cross College 21-20 in the Vodafone Super Deans Eliminations Competition in Suva today.

Holy Cross College dominated the opening half, putting pressure on the Southern Zone finalists from the first whistle and taking a commanding 17-0 lead into the break.

However, Nasinu returned after half-time with renewed determination, showing composure and resilience to turn the match around.

The team scored 21 unanswered points in the second half to secure a dramatic one-point victory and book a place in the national quarter-finals.

The match ended with emotional scenes as Holy Cross players struggled to come to terms with surrendering their first-half advantage and allowing Nasinu to complete a memorable comeback.

In other results, Cuvu College thumped Saint John Cawaci 55-7, while Suva Grammar School beat Ratu Luke Secondary School 50-6.

Lelean Memorial School defeated Marist Brothers High School 26-7, while Ratu Kadavulevu School thrashed Ratu Sukuna Memorial School 43-14 to secure their places in the national quarter-finals.

item.title: Lack of scoreboard sparks debate at Super Deans
item.description: A dramatic finish to the Vodafone Super Deans Under-18 elimination match between Holy Cross College and Nasinu Secondary School has reignited calls for scoreboards to become a standard feature at secondary school rugby fixtures. item.content:encoded:
A dramatic finish to the Vodafone Super Deans Under-18 elimination match between Holy Cross College and Nasinu Secondary School has reignited calls for scoreboards to become a standard feature at secondary school rugby fixtures.

A parent from Wairiki told fijivillage News that Fiji has reached Tier One status in international rugby, yet at the grassroots level schools still cannot afford a proper scoreboard to keep players informed of the score.

The parent says a scoreboard does more than display the score; it provides players, coaches, match officials and spectators with accurate, real-time information that can influence tactical decisions and reduce confusion during crucial moments of a game.

He says in knockout rugby, where every point matters, knowing whether a team is leading or trailing often determines how the final minutes are played.

Holy Cross College's campaign came to a heartbreaking end after one of their players kicked the ball into touch, believing his side was leading against Southern Zone finalists Nasinu Secondary School.

Unaware of the actual score, the player attempted to end the match by putting the ball into touch, only to discover that his team was, in fact, trailing Nasinu Secondary School 21-20.

The costly mistake left players, officials and spectators stunned, with many pointing to the absence of a visible scoreboard as a contributing factor.

While players are expected to maintain awareness during matches, school rugby coaches and supporters say the incident highlights a gap that can easily be addressed through better match-day facilities.

The Holy Cross incident has sparked discussion among rugby supporters about whether tournament organisers should prioritise portable electronic or manual scoreboards at all competition venues, as incidents like this happen every year.

As school rugby continues to grow in popularity and competitiveness, many believe providing accurate score information should become a basic requirement rather than a luxury.

Southern Zone Rugby President, Rusiate Wadali told fijivillage News that the board will get a scoreboard next year.

item.title: Extra Premier League: Ba extend lead at the top with thrilling 2-1 victory over Labasa
item.description: Ba coach Ravinesh Kumar described the match as a tough contest against a strong Labasa side, saying his team remained patient and stuck to its game plan. Kumar says the match highlighted areas for improvement, but the team learned from its mistakes and will continue to improve.
item.content:encoded:
Ba coach Ravinesh Kumar described the match as a tough contest against a strong Labasa side, saying his team remained patient and stuck to its game plan.

Kumar says the match highlighted areas for improvement, but the team learned from its mistakes and will continue to improve.

He says his half-time message was to keep possession, use the flanks effectively and remain patient, and the players' response helped them score the winning goal in the final minute.

Meanwhile, before the men's clash, Labasa Women thrashed Ba Women 6-1 in a Digicel Women's Super League match.

Nadi claimed a vital 3-2 victory over Nasinu at Uprising Sports Ground.

In tomorrow's matches, Tailevu Naitasiri will host Navua at Uprising Sports Ground at 1pm.

Rewa will face Suva at 1pm at Churchill Park, before Lautoka take on Nadroga at 3pm.

item.title: Infantino scraps controversial FIFA investment plan after backlash
item.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has withdrawn his controversial proposal to sell minority stakes in the governing body's major competitions after widespread opposition from football's regional confederations. Infantino says it had become clear the proposal had created divisions that were no longer in the interest of its original objective.
item.content:encoded:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino has withdrawn his controversial proposal to sell minority stakes in the governing body's major competitions after widespread opposition from football's regional confederations.

Infantino says it had become clear the proposal had created divisions that were no longer in the interest of its original objective.

He says, as a result, this proposal will not proceed.

The proposal would have seen FIFA create a new commercial subsidiary to manage its major competitions, including the men's and women's FIFA World Cups, with private investors able to buy minority stakes.

Infantino had also offered FIFA's 211 member associations up to US$40 million in future funding if they supported the proposal.

However, UEFA's 55 member associations voted to boycott FIFA World Cups if the plan went ahead, while Concacaf rejected the proposal and the Asian Football Confederation backed UEFA and Concacaf's position.

FIFA Chief Operating Officer Kevin Lamour also admitted the organisation's administration had been deceived about the project.

Infantino says he will now work to bring all interested parties back together in the spirit of shared interest in football.

The FIFA President is seeking re-election for a fourth term at the 77th FIFA Congress in March next year.

item.title: Labasa Sanatan Tournament: Nasea Sanatan set up quarter-final clash with Emily Sanatan
item.description: Mohammed Feroz , Priya Nand · 01/08/2026 Defending champions Nasea Sanatan have advanced to the quarter-finals of the CK Mega Bargain Labasa Sanatan Tournament 2026 after defeating Naleba Sanatan in a penalty shootout at Subrail Park.
item.content:encoded:
Mohammed Feroz , Priya Nand · 01/08/2026

Defending champions Nasea Sanatan have advanced to the quarter-finals of the CK Mega Bargain Labasa Sanatan Tournament 2026 after defeating Naleba Sanatan in a penalty shootout at Subrail Park.

The match ended goalless after regulation time, with both teams creating chances but failing to find the back of the net.

Naleba came close to breaking the deadlock when a powerful shot struck the post, while Nasea controlled possession with their short-passing game.

Naleba featured former Labasa representative Vikaran Chandra in attack, while former Seaqaqa representative Roneet produced a strong defensive performance to keep Nasea under pressure.

Nasea Sanatan captain and current Nasinu representative Shalvesh Singh says his side is pleased to have advanced to the quarter-finals.

He says they are taking one game at a time.

Meanwhile, Fiji international Roy Krishna helped Emily Sanatan secure a victory over Cogeloa Shiv Shakti Sanatan, scoring a stunning 40-yard strike in their knockout match.

Dogoloa produced an impressive performance and created several chances but could not find an equaliser before the final whistle.

However, Emily Sanatan will be without Krishna for their quarter-final clash against Nasea Sanatan after the Fiji star was sent off after receiving his second yellow card of the match.

The highly anticipated quarter-final between Emily Sanatan and Nasea Sanatan will be played this evening at Subrail Park.

item.title: A dream realised: Terio Tamani earns his Kadavu call-up
item.description: For current Fiji Airways Men's National 7s scrum-half Terio Tamani, wearing the Kadavu Rugby Union jersey has always been more than a goal, it has been a dream. The Kadavu Rugby Union says that earlier this year, they had looked forward to seeing Tamani in their starting line-up for the Koroturaga Cup quarter-final against Queen Victoria School Old Boys.
item.content:encoded:
For current Fiji Airways Men's National 7s scrum-half Terio Tamani, wearing the Kadavu Rugby Union jersey has always been more than a goal, it has been a dream.

The Kadavu Rugby Union says that earlier this year, they had looked forward to seeing Tamani in their starting line-up for the Koroturaga Cup quarter-final against Queen Victoria School Old Boys.

They say circumstances beyond their control prevented him from taking the field.

The Union says that today, that dream finally becomes a reality.

Tamani will proudly wear the No. 9 jersey for Kadavu as they face Nadi in their opening Skipper Cup match.

They say this milestone is a testament to his patience, perseverance, hard work and unwavering dedication to the game.

Kadavu will take on Nadi in round one of the Skipper Cup at King Charles Park in Nadi at 11am today.

In other matches, Rewa will face Naitasiri at the Burebasaga Ground at 11am, while Lautoka will host Nadroga at Churchill Park, also at 11am.

Meanwhile, Suva edged Ba 28-26 yesterday.

item.title: Ba and Labasa battle for top spot in Extra Premier League
item.description: Ba FC and Labasa FC will go head-to-head in a crucial Extra Premier League clash at 2pm today at Subrail Park. Just one point separates the two teams, with Ba leading the standings on 33 points and Labasa close behind on 32.
item.content:encoded:
Ba FC and Labasa FC will go head-to-head in a crucial Extra Premier League clash at 2pm today at Subrail Park.

Just one point separates the two teams, with Ba leading the standings on 33 points and Labasa close behind on 32.

Defending champions Rewa FC are third on 29 points, making today's result crucial in the title race.

A win for Ba would extend its lead to four points with only two matches remaining and move the Men in Black a step closer to a record-extending 22nd league title.

Labasa, meanwhile, knows that a home victory would see the Babasiga Lions climb to the top of the table and take control of the title race heading into the final rounds.

The match also carries added significance for Ba, which is chasing its first league title since the 2018-19 season after already winning the 2026 BiC Fiji FACT.

Meanwhile, before the men's clash, Labasa Women FC is taking on the unbeaten Ba Women FC in a Digicel Women's Super League match.

Nadi FC claimed a vital 3-2 victory over Nasinu FC in their clash at Uprising Sports Ground.

In tomorrow's matches, Tailevu Naitasiri FC will host Navua FC at Uprising Sports Ground at 1pm.

Rewa FC will face Suva FC at 1pm at Churchill Park before Lautoka FC takes on Nadroga FC at 3pm.

item.title: Vodafone Super Deans Eliminations: QVS knocked out after draw
item.description: Queen Victoria School has been eliminated from the Fiji Secondary Schools Vodafone Super Deans Eliminations competition after drawing 29-29 with Ba Provincial Free Bird Institute. According to the competition organisers, Ba Provincial Free Bird Institute advanced because they scored the first points of the match, which served as the tiebreaker.
item.content:encoded:
Queen Victoria School has been eliminated from the Fiji Secondary Schools Vodafone Super Deans Eliminations competition after drawing 29-29 with Ba Provincial Free Bird Institute.

According to the competition organisers, Ba Provincial Free Bird Institute advanced because they scored the first points of the match, which served as the tiebreaker.

In another result, Suva Grammar School's Under-16 side secured a convincing 39-7 victory over Labasa College.

Upcoming fixtures at Grammar Ground will see Holy Cross College take on Nasinu Secondary School at 12.20pm, followed by Suva Grammar School against Ratu Luke Secondary School at 1.50pm.

At St Vincent Ground, Lelean Memorial School will face Marist Brothers High School at 12.20pm, while Ratu Kadavulevu School will meet Ratu Sukuna Memorial School at 1.50pm.

Cuvu College will face St John's College at 1.00pm.

Meanwhile, at Ratu Ganilau Park, Ratu Navula College will take on Shiri Guru Nanak Khalsa College at 2pm before Ra High School faces Navatu Secondary School at 3.25pm.
